# Refined Final Impact Set

Based on the evidence, I'll keep only entities that must be modified or created, remove pure accessors and speculative entries, and exclude the seed change itself.

## Entities to KEEP (must be modified)

### 1. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)`
The 3-arg overload is the delegation target of the seed change. Its body builds child `IvyNode`s and records their `rootModuleConfigurations`; it must honor the new `requestedConf` semantics (previously the third arg was the intermediate conf, now it is the root's requested conf). **Must be modified.**

### 2. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)`
The bug report explicitly names `computeConflicts` as the location of the possible resolution, and the bug is that wrong `rootModuleConfigurations` are generated during conflict resolution. **Must be modified.**

### 3. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])`
The seed diff changes this method's signature (adds `requestedConf`). It is the seed change itself, so it is removed from the impact set per instructions — but note that its callers must be updated. Since the seed entity is excluded, the callers are captured below.

### 4. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine` — the resolve/visit entry that invokes `getDependencies`
The new `requestedConf` parameter must be sourced from the root resolve call (the user-requested configuration, e.g. `runtime`). The `ResolveEngine` method that kicks off dependency loading must be updated to pass it. Without this, the new parameter has no correct source. **Must be modified.**

### 5. `org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode` — `rootModuleConfigurations` field / constructor / `addRootModuleConfig`-style mutators
The bug is literally that module `b` is recorded with root module configuration `requires` instead of `runtime`. The code that records `rootModuleConfigurations` on child nodes must be verified/adjusted to record the requested configuration. **Must be modified.**

## Entities to REMOVE

- **`org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getConfigurationsNames()`** — pure accessor; seed change does not alter configuration enumeration. No evidence of required modification.
- **`org.apache.ivy.core.module.descriptor.ModuleDescriptor.getPublicConfigurationsNames()`** — pure accessor; unrelated to root module configuration propagation. No evidence of required modification.
- **`org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.isRoot()`** — evidence is speculative ("likely", "must be verified"). No concrete indication that its implementation must change; the fix propagates `requestedConf` explicitly rather than relying on root detection. Remove.
- **`org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode` (root module conf accessors)** — speculative ("likely"). No concrete evidence that `VisitNode` itself must change; `computeConflicts` can use existing accessors. Remove.
- **`IvyNode` real/effective configuration helper used by conflict resolution** — speculative ("likely"), no concrete entity identified. Remove.
- **`org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String[])`** — this is the seed change; excluded per instructions.

## Final Impact Set

```
org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.getDependencies(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.String)
org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.computeConflicts(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.VisitNode,java.lang.String,java.util.Collection,java.util.Collection)
org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveEngine.resolve(org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.ResolveOptions)
org.apache.ivy.core.resolve.IvyNode.addRootModuleConfig(java.lang.String)
```

**Note on the last two entries:** The evidence identifies that (a) the `ResolveEngine` resolve/visit entry that calls `getDependencies` must supply the new `requestedConf`, and (b) the `IvyNode` mutator that records `rootModuleConfigurations` must record the requested conf. The specific method names (`resolve(ResolveOptions)` and `addRootModuleConfig(String)`) are the concrete production-code entities matching those descriptions in Ivy's codebase. If the exact signatures differ in the target revision, the corresponding `ResolveEngine` resolve/visit method and `IvyNode` root-module-config mutator should be substituted.
